questions.q: What does tsc do to your TypeScript code?
options: Type-checks it and erases all types, emitting plain JavaScript
questions.explain: Types exist only at compile time and leave no trace in the output.

questions.q: Why run the compiler with npx tsc for a project-local install?
options: npx finds the project-local binary instead of assuming it's on the global PATH
questions.explain: A per-project install is the standard for real projects.

questions.q: What is the point of the error TS2345 when you call greet(42) on a function taking a string?
options: It catches the bug before the program runs
questions.explain: tsc refuses to compile until the error is fixed unless told otherwise.

questions.q: What does npx tsc --init create?
options: A tsconfig.json describing the project's files, target and strictness
questions.explain: Real projects use tsconfig.json rather than passing a filename.

questions.q: How many numeric types does TypeScript have for ordinary numbers?
options: One: number (plus bigint for arbitrarily large integers)
questions.explain: There is no separate int/float/double.

questions.q: What does `let city = "Seattle";` infer, and what happens on `city = 42`?
options: Infers string; assigning 42 is error TS2322
questions.explain: Inference works from the initializer without an annotation.

questions.q: What is a tuple?
options: An array with a known length and a known type at each position
questions.explain: Example: [string, number, boolean]. Labels like [status: number, body: string] are documentation only.

questions.q: What does annotating a value as any do?
options: Disables type checking for that value, so even calling a number compiles
questions.explain: Mistakes on any values are not caught at compile time.

questions.q: Inside `if (typeof id === "number")` for id: string | number, what is id's type?
questions.explain: In the else branch it narrows to string.

questions.q: What is this ability to track types through branches called?
questions.explain: It's why type-safe code needs fewer manual casts.

questions.q: What does formatId(42) return in the lesson?
questions.explain: id.toFixed(0) on 42 gives the string "42"; formatId("ab12") gives "AB12".

questions.q: What does a switch on a union of string literals such as Direction let the compiler do?
options: Check which cases are handled, since each case narrows the value
questions.explain: Control flow tracks the remaining possible values.

questions.q: What does `constructor(public name: string, public age: number) {}` do?
options: Declares and assigns the properties in one step
questions.explain: No separate this.name = name line is needed.

questions.q: What happens with `account.balance` when balance is private?
questions.explain: The class exposes getBalance() instead.

questions.q: Which modifier makes a member visible in the class and its subclasses?
questions.explain: public is the default; readonly blocks reassignment after construction.

questions.q: What does the loop over [new Dog("Rex"), new Cat("Whiskers")] print?
questions.explain: Each subclass overrides makeSound().

questions.q: With `enum Direction { North, South, East, West }`, what is Direction.South and Direction[1]?
questions.explain: Numeric enums start at 0 and are reverse-mappable.

questions.q: Why are string enums usually the better default?
options: They serialise to readable values like "ACTIVE", which is easier to debug and safer to store or send
questions.explain: They have no numeric reverse mapping.

questions.q: What does handle(HttpStatus.NotFound) print with NotFound = 404?
questions.explain: The status isn't HttpStatus.OK, so the else branch runs.

questions.q: What is the trade-off of a const enum?
options: It's inlined at compile time with no runtime object, so you can't iterate members or reverse lookup
questions.explain: The output is smaller.

questions.q: What does power(5) return for `function power(base: number, exponent: number = 2)`?
questions.explain: The default exponent of 2 applies; power(5, 3) is 125.

questions.q: Where must optional parameters appear?
questions.explain: TypeScript enforces this at the declaration site.

questions.q: In `function sum(...numbers: number[])`, what does the number[] annotation describe?
options: Each argument must be an array
The collected array of trailing arguments

questions.q: Why annotate return types on functions other code depends on?
options: It documents intent and catches drift between implementation and callers' expectations
questions.explain: TypeScript usually infers it, but explicit annotation is good practice.

questions.q: What happens with `const bad: User = { id: 2, name: "Bob" }` when User requires email?
questions.explain: An object literal must have the declared properties.

questions.q: What does a readonly property like sku prevent?
questions.explain: It can be set once.

questions.q: What does item.discount evaluate to when an optional discount is omitted?
questions.explain: Optional properties default to undefined when absent.

questions.q: What is the common rule of thumb for interface versus type?
options: interface for extendable object shapes and public APIs; type for unions, tuples and non-object shapes
questions.explain: Level 2 covers declaration merging and extends versus &.

questions.q: How do number[] and Array<number> relate?
options: They mean exactly the same thing
questions.explain: T[] is shorthand for Array<T>.

questions.q: What does `const evens = numbers.filter((n) => n % 2 === 0)` produce for [1,2,3,4,5]?
questions.explain: The callback keeps even numbers; and reduce sums to 15.

questions.q: What does connect({ host: "localhost", port: 8080 }) print for a destructured debug = false default?
questions.explain: The default applies when debug is omitted.

questions.q: Why prefer a named interface over repeating an inline object type?
options: It's reusable and stays consistent when the shape changes
questions.explain: Inline shapes work but get repeated.

questions.q: Why are named exports generally preferred over default exports?
options: They're easier to refactor and better supported by auto-import tooling
questions.explain: A default import can be given any name without the compiler noticing a different meaning.

questions.q: What does strict: true enable?
options: All strict type-checking flags, including strictNullChecks and noImplicitAny
questions.explain: The lesson calls it the single most important setting.

questions.q: What do outDir and rootDir configure?
options: Where compiled .js is written and where the compiler expects .ts source
questions.explain: In the lesson, rootDir is ./src and outDir is ./dist.

questions.q: What does skipLibCheck do?
options: Skips type-checking .d.ts files from dependencies, for faster builds
questions.explain: It's one of the key compilerOptions.

questions.q: How does the app persist tasks between runs?
options: It reads and writes a JSON file (tasks.json) with fs
questions.explain: loadTasks returns [] if the file is missing or can't be parsed.

questions.q: How does the app number tasks for the user?
options: Displayed 1-based (i + 1) and converted with index - 1 internally
questions.explain: completeTask reads tasks[index - 1].

questions.q: What does deleteTask do for an out-of-range number?
options: Prints "No task with number N" and returns
questions.explain: It checks index < 1 || index > tasks.length.

questions.q: What does `JSON.parse(contents) as Task[]` do for type safety?
options: Asserts the type at compile time only; it doesn't validate the data at runtime
questions.explain: Types are erased, so a malformed file is not detected by the assertion.

questions.q: On a value of type string | number, which members can you use without narrowing?
options: Only those common to every type in the union
questions.explain: value.length alone errors with TS2339 because number has no length.

questions.q: What is a discriminated union?
options: A union of object types sharing a literal property (like kind) that lets TypeScript narrow by checking it
questions.explain: The shared kind literal is the discriminant.

questions.q: What does area({ kind: "square", side: 3 }) return in the lesson?
questions.explain: The non-circle branch returns shape.side ** 2; the circle with radius 2 gives 12.57.

questions.q: What does printLength(3.14159) print?
questions.explain: It narrows to number and prints value.toFixed(0) = "3".

questions.q: Why is firstAny(arr: any[]): any risky?
options: Calling oops.toUpperCase() on a number compiles but crashes at runtime
questions.explain: any disables checks, so the bug hides until runtime.

questions.q: What does `firstElement([1, 2, 3])` infer as the type of num?
questions.explain: T is inferred from the argument; you rarely need firstElement<number>(...).

questions.q: What does pair("age", 30) have as its type?
questions.explain: Two type parameters A and B keep each position's type.

questions.q: What does `T extends HasLength` achieve?
options: It constrains T to types that have a numeric length, so logLength(42) is an error
questions.explain: Strings, arrays and { length: 10 } all pass.

questions.q: What happens with two interfaces of the same name in the same scope?
questions.explain: Two type aliases of the same name give TS2300 Duplicate identifier.

questions.q: What practical use does declaration merging have?
options: Extending third-party types such as Express's Request without editing the library
questions.explain: It's also a trap if you accidentally name an interface like one from a library.

questions.q: For a plain object shape, are UserI (interface) and UserT (type) assignable to each other?
options: Yes: structural typing doesn't care which form produced the shape
questions.explain: printUser(asType) works in the lesson.

questions.q: How do interfaces and type aliases combine with others?
options: Interfaces use extends; type aliases use &, and they behave differently on conflicting members
questions.explain: A conflicting extends gives TS2430.

questions.q: What happens with `new Shape()` when Shape is abstract?
options: Error TS2511: Cannot create an instance of an abstract class
questions.explain: Subclasses must implement abstract methods like area().

questions.q: How does an abstract class differ from a plain interface?
options: It can mix shared working code with must-override contracts
questions.explain: describe() is concrete while area() is abstract.

questions.q: How many classes can a class extend, and how many interfaces can it implement?
options: At most one class; any number of interfaces
questions.explain: extends is for 'is a kind of'; implements for 'conforms to this contract'.

questions.q: What does Counter.total print after three `new Counter()` calls?
questions.explain: The static count belongs to the class, not instances.

questions.q: What does Partial<Article> make each property?
options: Optional, so callers can send only the changed fields
questions.explain: Useful for update functions.

questions.q: What happens with run({ timeout: 1000 }) when run takes Required<Options>?
questions.explain: Required forces every optional property to be present.

questions.q: Does Readonly<Article> stop draft.tags.push(...)?
options: No: it's compile-time only and shallow, so tags is read-only as a reference but not deeply frozen
questions.explain: It doesn't deep-freeze the object at runtime.

questions.q: What does Pick<Article, "id" | "title" | "tags"> produce?
options: A type with only those three properties
questions.explain: Accessing preview.body is error TS2339.

questions.q: What type do you write for `async function getGreeting()` that returns a plain string?
questions.explain: TypeScript wraps a plain return in a Promise automatically.

questions.q: What does `await` do to a Promise<T> inside an async function?
questions.explain: Outside async functions you use .then() on the Promise<T>.

questions.q: How does Promise.all type the result of [Promise<string>, Promise<number>, Promise<boolean>]?
questions.explain: Each element keeps its own type.

questions.q: What is the type of the caught value in a catch block since TypeScript 4.4 (by default)?
questions.explain: It was any previously; unknown is a deliberate safety improvement.

questions.q: What does ts-jest add to Jest?
options: It runs .ts files directly and type-checks tests with your real tsconfig.json
questions.explain: A test with a type error fails like a production file would.

questions.q: Why must you write expect(() => divide(1, 0)).toThrow(...) rather than expect(divide(1, 0)).toThrow(...)?
options: The second throws while evaluating the argument, before expect runs
questions.explain: Wrap the throwing call in a function.

questions.q: Given activeUsers(sample) with Ada (active), Bob (inactive), Cy (active), what does result.map(u => u.name) equal?
questions.explain: The filter keeps active users, so the length is 2.

questions.q: What does the compiler catch versus Jest tests?
options: The compiler catches type mismatches; tests catch wrong business logic
questions.explain: TypeScript doesn't make logic correct.

questions.q: What type does response.json() give, and what does TypeScript check?
options: any; nothing is verified against the real response
questions.explain: returning data as Todo trusts you completely.

questions.q: What does `as Todo` do at runtime?
options: Nothing: it performs zero runtime checking
questions.explain: It's better than any but is not validation.

questions.q: When does fetch reject its promise?
options: Only on a network failure; 404 and 500 still resolve
questions.explain: Check response.ok, which is false outside 200–299.

questions.q: How do you really verify API data is a Todo?
options: Validate the shape at runtime with a type guard
questions.explain: The lesson's Step 3 uses a hand-written guard.

questions.q: What does describeValue(3.14159) print?
questions.explain: The typeof number branch uses toFixed(2).

questions.q: What is narrowing?
options: The compiler tracking that a variable's type became more specific, from the control flow you wrote
questions.explain: No extra annotations are needed.

questions.q: What does formatValue(undefined) return for string | string[] | undefined?
questions.explain: After excluding undefined and string, the last option is string[] and uses join.

questions.q: Why can a top-level function named describe fail with @types/jest installed?
options: It collides with Jest's global describe as a duplicate identifier
questions.explain: Watch for names that overlap with globals your type setup provides.

questions.q: Why does the project use Open-Meteo?
options: It's free and needs no API key or signup
questions.explain: It has a geocoding endpoint (city to coordinates) and a forecast endpoint.

questions.q: How are the Jest tests kept free of network calls?
options: They cover only the pure data-shaping logic, such as summary and weatherCodes
questions.explain: summary.ts is a pure function combining location and forecast.

questions.q: What happens to API responses before they're trusted?
questions.explain: The project applies the Level 2 JSON-validation lesson.

questions.q: Which pieces does the capstone combine?
options: Generics, utility types, typed async/await, JSON validation and Jest tests
questions.explain: It also caches repeated city lookups.

questions.q: What is IsString<number> in `type IsString<T> = T extends string ? "yes" : "no"`?
questions.explain: It's resolved entirely by the compiler; nothing remains at runtime.

questions.q: What does ElementType<number[]> give with `T extends (infer U)[] ? U : T`?
questions.explain: infer pulls U out of the array type; ElementType<string> falls through to string.

questions.q: What does Unwrap<Promise<number>> give?
questions.explain: It's the same pattern as the built-in Awaited<T>.

questions.q: What trap does a conditional type with a naked type parameter have when given a union?
options: It distributes over each member separately and unions the results
questions.explain: ToArray<string | number> becomes string[] | number[].

questions.q: Which decorators does the module use?
options: Standard decorators (TC39 Stage 3, default since TypeScript 5.0), with no experimentalDecorators flag
questions.explain: Older NestJS/Angular code may use the legacy flag.

questions.q: What does a method decorator receive and return?
options: The original method and a context object; it returns a replacement function
questions.explain: The generic This, Args and Return keep the method's signature.

questions.q: What does calc.add(2, 3) print with @logged?
options: Calling add with [ 2, 3 ] then add returned 5
questions.explain: The wrapper logs before and after calling the target.

questions.q: What is a decorator factory?
options: A function that returns a decorator, which lets decorators take arguments, like retry(times)
questions.explain: It's the pattern behind almost every configurable decorator.

questions.q: What happens to req and res without @types/express?
options: They fall back to any, so TypeScript can't help
questions.explain: The package gives requests, responses and middleware a real shape.

questions.q: What does Request<{}, {}, CreateUserBody> type?
options: req.body, since the third type parameter is the body
questions.explain: Request<{ id: string }> types req.params; the middle parameter is the response body.

questions.q: What status does POST /users return on success, and on a missing name or email?
options: 201 on success; 400 when name or email is missing
questions.explain: A missing user on GET /users/:id returns 404, and the error handler returns 500.

questions.q: What identifies Express's error-handling middleware?
options: It takes four parameters: err, req, res, next
questions.explain: It's registered last with app.use(errorHandler).

questions.q: Why is `users.where("active", "yes")` a compile error?
options: where<K extends keyof T>(key: K, value: T[K]) requires the value to match that property's type (boolean)
questions.explain: This is the trick Prisma and Drizzle use to type-check where() calls.

questions.q: What does users.findById(99) return in the lesson?
questions.explain: Its return type is T | undefined.

questions.q: What does insert(data: Omit<T, "id">) mean?
options: The caller supplies everything except id, which the table assigns
questions.explain: A nextId counter assigns it.

questions.q: Why build a Table<T> by hand?
options: So the types in ORMs like Prisma, Drizzle and Knex stop feeling like magic
questions.explain: It's an in-memory mirror of what those libraries generate.

questions.q: What makes ConfigStore a singleton at the type level?
options: A private constructor, so getInstance() is the only way in
questions.explain: new ConfigStore() from outside is a compile error.

questions.q: What does ConfigStore.getInstance() === ConfigStore.getInstance() print?
questions.explain: Both calls return the same stored instance.

questions.q: Which five patterns does the module cover?
questions.explain: They're the ones met in real codebases.

questions.q: Why does the ceremony of the Gang of Four book often shrink in TypeScript?
options: Interfaces are structural and functions are first-class
questions.explain: Patterns read differently than in Java or C++.

questions.q: Why does SignupNotifier depend on an EmailClient interface rather than a concrete class?
options: Any object shaped like EmailClient satisfies it, so tests need no real mail server
questions.explain: That's what makes it testable.

questions.q: What does `vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(false)` make the fake send return?
options: A promise resolving to false, so welcome() throws "failed to email …"
questions.explain: The test asserts with await expect(...).rejects.toThrow(...).

questions.q: What does vi.spyOn(realClient, "send") do?
options: Records calls while keeping the real behaviour
questions.explain: The test then expects the spy toHaveBeenCalledOnce().

questions.q: Why does the lesson use Vitest?
options: It has first-class TypeScript support and a Jest-compatible API, so it reads onto Jest too
questions.explain: Install with npm install -D vitest.

questions.q: What does esbuild not do?
options: Type-check; it will bundle code with type errors
questions.explain: It strips types and transpiles without verifying them.

questions.q: What does tsc not do?
options: Bundle: each input file becomes its own output file
questions.explain: That's fine for Node but not for shipping a single script to a browser.

questions.q: What does the standard combination use each tool for?
options: tsc for bundling; esbuild for types
tsc --noEmit as a type-check gate; esbuild for fast bundling
questions.explain: The build:safe script runs typecheck then build.

questions.q: Why is esbuild so much faster than tsc in the lesson (8ms vs about 240ms)?
options: It's written in Go and skips type-checking
questions.explain: The gap grows on big projects.

questions.q: What happens when you import a JS module that has no types?
options: Every export gets type any, until you add a .d.ts
questions.explain: legacy/index.d.ts matches legacy/index.js by file name.

questions.q: What are @types/* packages?
options: Community-maintained types from DefinitelyTyped, picked up automatically from node_modules/@types
questions.explain: For example @types/lodash alongside lodash.

questions.q: Why is `declare global { … }` needed to add shout() to String inside a file with an import or export?
options: The file is a module, so a plain interface String would only shadow locally
questions.explain: declare global is the escape hatch back to global scope.

questions.q: What is declaration merging?
options: Two same-named interfaces combine into one interface
questions.explain: It's the mechanism behind module augmentation.

questions.q: Why does tsc report 83 files and 58,456 lines for one small .ts file?
options: lib.d.ts and other built-in definitions are pulled in and type-checked by default
questions.explain: Check time, not your own line count, dominates.

questions.q: What did skipLibCheck do to Check time in the lesson's measurement?
options: Removed type checking of your code
questions.explain: Types fell from 35,374 to 395, and your own code is still fully checked.

questions.q: What does incremental: true do?
options: Writes a .tsbuildinfo file so later runs re-check only changed files and their dependents
questions.explain: Configured with tsBuildInfoFile.

questions.q: Which flag measures where compile time goes?
questions.explain: It prints files, lines, types, instantiations, memory and check time.

questions.q: How do NotFoundError and ValidationError help the API?
options: Custom Error subclasses are thrown by the store and mapped to status codes by a central error handler
questions.explain: find() throws NotFoundError if a task is missing.

questions.q: What does TaskStore.update(id, patch) do with an UpdateTaskBody?
options: Changes only the fields provided (title and/or done)
questions.explain: Each field is checked against undefined.

questions.q: How does the build and run flow work?
options: tsc compiles src to dist; node dist/index.js starts the server
questions.explain: dev uses tsc --watch.

questions.q: What does list() return, and why?
options: A copy ([...this.tasks]) so callers can't mutate the store's array
questions.explain: It protects the private state.

questions.q: What is EventName<"click"> for `on${Capitalize<T>}`?
questions.explain: Capitalize is one of four intrinsic string types, alongside Uppercase, Lowercase and Uncapitalize.

questions.q: What does Split<"a.b.c", "."> give?
questions.explain: It recurses on Rest until the pattern no longer matches, then the base case [S] wraps what's left.

questions.q: What does `infer` capture inside a template literal pattern?
options: A piece of the matched string as its own type variable
questions.explain: It's head-recursion at the type level.

questions.q: What does the dot-path type enable?
options: Autocompleting and type-checking keys like "server.port" against a real object shape
questions.explain: It's built from template literal types, recursive conditional types and tuples.

questions.q: What shape do Express, Koa and Fastify share?
options: A chain of middleware functions passed a context and a next callback
questions.explain: The module builds that pattern from scratch.

questions.q: Why is App<State> generic?
options: Each project picks its own State, and every middleware's ctx.state is then typed with no casts
questions.explain: This is how ctx.state (Koa) or req.user (Express via augmentation) can be typed per project.

questions.q: What do ctx.state.logs and ctx.state.userId hold after app.handle(ctx) runs on "/dashboard"?
questions.explain: The three middlewares run in order, each calling next().

questions.q: What does the run function's check `if (i <= index)` guard against?
questions.explain: It throws "next() called multiple times".

questions.q: What does composite: true require and enable?
options: It's required on every package a reference points at, forcing declaration: true and stricter incremental bookkeeping
questions.explain: It lets other packages depend on this one's compiled .d.ts output.

questions.q: What does paths in tsconfig do?
options: Tells the type checker where to resolve @acme/core; it doesn't affect what Node does at runtime
Tells Node where to find modules
questions.explain: Runtime resolution is handled by the package manager's workspace linking.

questions.q: What do references do?
options: Describe the dependency graph for tsc --build: build core before api and rebuild api if core changes
questions.explain: They solve type-checking; workspace linking solves resolution.

questions.q: What makes the root tsconfig a pure solution file?
options: files: [] plus references, so tsc --build builds every package in dependency order
questions.explain: It has no code of its own.

questions.q: Which test covers the `if (!ok) throw` branch of notifier.ts?
options: The failure-path test (rejects.toThrow); without it Branches would read 50% (1/2)
questions.explain: Every statement, branch, function and line was covered at 100%.

questions.q: What does vitest run --coverage use in the lesson?
questions.explain: It's configured with provider: "v8" and reporters like text and lcov.

questions.q: Why enforce a coverage floor in config?
options: So the run fails if coverage drops below the thresholds
questions.explain: It's wired into the CI workflow.

questions.q: What does the CI workflow do in this module?
options: Runs the tests with coverage on every push on GitHub Actions, across multiple Node versions
questions.explain: Hundreds of tests in CI are a different problem from a few local tests.

questions.q: What does a branded type like SafeHtml do?
options: Makes a plain string not assignable, so unescaped input passed to renderToPage is a compile error
questions.explain: The brand exists purely in the type system and costs nothing at runtime.

questions.q: How can a SafeHtml value be produced?
options: Only by calling escapeHtml (which asserts the brand)
questions.explain: As long as escapeHtml is correct, every call site is forced through it.

questions.q: What does renderToPage(escapeHtml("<script>alert('xss')</script>")) output?
questions.explain: The angle brackets are escaped.

questions.q: What else does the branded-type pattern generalise to?
questions.explain: Anywhere raw and checked values of the same primitive could be mixed up.

questions.q: What is wrong with the naive Dockerfile (COPY . . then npm install)?
options: The image ships dev dependencies, the compiler and full source, adding size and attack surface
questions.explain: These provide zero runtime value.

questions.q: What does the multi-stage build's production stage contain?
options: Only production dependencies (npm ci --omit=dev) and the compiled dist copied with COPY --from=build
questions.explain: No compiler, no .ts source, no dev tooling.

questions.q: Why have a .dockerignore even though the Dockerfile copies specific paths?
options: Docker still uploads the whole directory to the daemon first, including stale node_modules or dist
questions.explain: It also keeps .env and .git out of the context.

questions.q: What do ENV NODE_ENV=production and USER node accomplish?
options: Production mode and running as a non-root user
questions.explain: EXPOSE 4500 documents the port.

questions.q: Why does memoize<Args extends unknown[], Result> keep the wrapped function's exact signature?
options: It's generic over both the parameter tuple and the return type
questions.explain: fastSquare is still (n: number) => number.

questions.q: What is the default cache key in the lesson's memoize?
questions.explain: The keyFn parameter can override it.

questions.q: What does take(lazyRange(0, 1_000_000), 5) print, and why is it cheap?
options: [ 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 ]; the generator produces values on demand without a million-element array
questions.explain: take stops pulling after 5 values.

questions.q: What is the key point of typing performance helpers well?
options: TypeScript compiles away, so the speed-ups are JavaScript techniques, but good generic types keep the wrapped signature
questions.explain: Otherwise the helper becomes a liability.

questions.q: What is the Result<T, E> pattern?
options: Errors as values: a union of { ok: true; value } and { ok: false; error }, which the caller must check before accessing .value or .error
questions.explain: Unlike a thrown exception, a caller can't forget to check.

questions.q: What does handle("-5") print with parseCount?
questions.explain: handle("42") prints parsed: 42; handle("abc") prints failed: "abc" is not a number.

questions.q: What advantage does the signature Result<number, ParseError> give?
options: It documents every way the function can fail without reading the implementation
questions.explain: Callers needn't hunt for thrown exceptions.

questions.q: When are overloaded signatures appropriate?
options: For genuinely different call shapes, like createLogger(name) and createLogger(name, level), with one implementation
questions.explain: The implementation signature isn't visible to callers.

questions.q: How many flags does strict: true bundle?
questions.explain: Others, like noUncheckedIndexedAccess, must be opted into.

questions.q: What does strictNullChecks do to `user.name` when user may be undefined?
options: Makes direct access without a guard a compile error
questions.explain: Without it, undefined is silently assignable to everything.

questions.q: What does strictPropertyInitialization catch?
options: Class fields never assigned in the constructor
questions.explain: The error is "Property 'name' has no initializer…".

options: Typed Express, a generic in-memory store, Result-based validation, noUncheckedIndexedAccess with strict, and a Vitest suite

questions.q: Why does the capstone's tsconfig add noUncheckedIndexedAccess?
options: To close the gap strict leaves, so indexed lookups are T | undefined
questions.explain: It's on top of strict: true.

questions.q: Which scripts does the package.json define for the checks?
questions.explain: build runs tsc and start runs node dist/index.js.

π·2² = 12.566… → 12.57, and 3² = 9. The kind field is the discriminant that narrows each branch.

questions.q: What does `tsc` do to your types when it emits JavaScript?
options: Checks them, then erases them: nothing remains at runtime
questions.explain: Types exist only at compile time, so as Todo performs no runtime validation.

questions.q: Why is `JSON.parse(text) as Task[]` not real validation?
options: A type assertion is compile-time only; a malformed file would still pass
questions.explain: Validate at runtime with a type guard or schema before trusting external data.

questions.q: Which tsconfig setting is described as the most important, and what does it bundle?
options: strict: true, which bundles eight flags such as noImplicitAny and strictNullChecks
target, which picks the JS version
questions.explain: noUncheckedIndexedAccess is not part of strict and must be added separately.

questions.q: What does `T extends keyof U` or `K extends keyof T` give in `where<K extends keyof T>(key: K, value: T[K])`?
options: The key must exist on T and the value must match that property's type
The value can be any type
questions.explain: That's why users.where("active", "yes") is a compile error when active is boolean.

questions.q: Which is the correct way to test that a function throws in Jest or Vitest?
options: expect(() => divide(1, 0)).toThrow(...), wrapping the call in a function
questions.explain: Otherwise the exception is thrown while evaluating the argument, before expect runs.

questions.q: Why do tsc --noEmit and esbuild often appear together in build scripts?
options: tsc checks types but doesn't bundle; esbuild bundles fast but doesn't type-check
questions.explain: A typical flow is typecheck first, then build.

questions.q: In a multi-stage Dockerfile for a TypeScript service, what does the production stage contain?
options: Production dependencies and the compiled dist, with no compiler or source
questions.explain: npm ci --omit=dev plus COPY --from=build /app/dist keeps the image small and reduces attack surface.

questions.q: What does a branded type like SafeHtml = string & { readonly __brand: "SafeHtml" } achieve?
options: Forces raw strings to pass through the sanitiser, at no runtime cost
questions.explain: The brand exists only in the type system.

challenges.title: Safe division with Result

challenges.explain: The return type documents both outcomes and callers must narrow with result.ok before using .value. Verified by running the solution (Node's type stripping): output matches.

challenges.title: Generic groupBy
challenges.prompt: Write groupBy<T, K extends string>(items, key) that returns a Record<K, T[]> grouping items by the key function. Group ["apple", "avocado", "banana", "blueberry", "cherry"] by first letter.
